user_ai_permissions.grain: One user's AI entitlements — which models they may reach, which one they get by default, and how the request is shaped. One row per user, or none.

governance.note: Read by `capabilities_for_user()` into the `models` block of its result, which is what the chat surfaces use to decide what to offer. Not part of the four capability layers — a capability answers "may you", this answers "with what".

columns.name: user_id
columns.meaning: The user these entitlements belong to. PK, so a user has at most one row.

columns.name: allowed_model_ids
columns.meaning: The models this user may use, as `ai_models.id`. An allow-list, but read as one only when it is non-empty.

substitutions.when: the array is empty, or the user has no row at all
substitutions.visible_as: nowhere, and it is worth stating plainly: EMPTY MEANS EVERYTHING here, not nothing. The resolver sets `all_allowed` true when the array is empty or absent, which preserves the behaviour that existed before the column did. An administrator clearing the list to revoke access would grant all of it instead.

columns.name: default_model_id
columns.meaning: The model a new conversation starts on. Nullable — the app falls back to its own default.

columns.name: fallback_model_id
columns.meaning: The model used when the default is unavailable or over budget.

columns.name: temperature
columns.meaning: Per-user sampling temperature override. Dimensionless and NOT a physical quantity — it is a model knob, recorded here so nobody mistakes it for one of the platform's measured values.

columns.name: max_context_override
columns.meaning: A per-user cap on context window size, in tokens. Nullable — the model's own limit applies.
columns.note: NOT TRACED into the simulation engine and never will be: `scsim` has no concept of a language model. This is an AI-plane setting that happens to live in the governance tier.

columns.name: created_at
columns.meaning: When the row was created. Server-stamped.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.meaning: When it was last changed. Server-stamped.

user_ai_permissions.note: The empty-array-means-everything rule in `allowed_model_ids` is the one thing a reader of this table must not get wrong. It is deliberate — it preserves the pre-column behaviour for every user who has no row — but it inverts the usual reading of an allow-list, and nothing at the point of display says so (§5 T2).

user_capabilities.grain: One grant or denial, for one user_id and one capability. The INNERMOST layer: an explicit per-person answer that beats every other.

governance.note: One of the four layers `capabilities_for_user()` resolves, in the order role -> org -> project -> user, most specific winning. `audited: false` and it matters here more than on most tables: these rows ARE the permissions, and a change to one currently leaves no record of who made it (§2.1 `audit-actor`, WP 2.3).

columns.name: user_id
columns.meaning: the user the row grants for.

columns.name: capability_key
columns.meaning: The capability, naming a row in `capabilities`.

columns.name: allowed
columns.meaning: Whether this layer grants the capability. TRI-STATE in effect: a missing row means "inherit from the next layer out", `false` means "deny here". They are different answers and the resolver's COALESCE depends on the difference.

substitutions.when: no row exists at this layer
substitutions.value: the next layer out decides; the chain ends in false
substitutions.visible_as: capabilities_for_user returns the resolved boolean; which layer decided is not reported

columns.name: created_at
columns.meaning: When the row was created. Server-stamped.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.meaning: When it was last changed. Server-stamped.

user_capabilities.note: WP 2.2 seeded `data_edit_inputs` and `data_edit_policies` into this table from whatever `data_editing` already said, so effective access on the day of deploy was identical to the day before. `data_editing` is deliberately still here: it is removed when the last call site has moved to one of the new keys, not before.
